title: The Pink coat of the girl
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：pink　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pink 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the guide wrote of ① a pink coat of the girl in the guidebook, and everybody in the valley said at once that it was ② pinker than the one named there the year before. Three days on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the guide, who never explained anything, had done it before dawn and gone home; it was the pink ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the pinkest coat of the girl anybody in the valley had ever seen, or so the guidebook for July 1972 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too pink to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the traveller who had come to help; the pink ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the map at the far ledge, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a pink light of the morning, and said that no traveller in his right mind would call it ⑥ as pink as the light of the morning they had once had in the old valley. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was pink or not, and he said so.

By 1985 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the guidebook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something pink, and nothing besides. The traveller from the next valley called the whole plan ⑧ quite pink; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the guidebook kept the names of the pink ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1988, in public, she wrote of another pink coat of the girl in the same guidebook, and the work, which took two days, seemed ⑨ pinker than anybody had expected. ⑩ The pinkest light of the morning in the whole valley, she said in 1990, was the one she could never quite name; the pink ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 粉色（前置定语 a pink coat of the girl：1978 年向导在旅行手册里记下的那件粉色的外套）
B. adj. 粉色／淡红（比较级 pinker than：文中两处，一处比姑娘的粉色外套，一处比预想）
C. adj. 粉色／淡红（最高级 the pinkest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 粉色（表语 too pink to do：母亲觉得它太粉色，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 淡红（前置定语 a pink light of the morning：叔叔把整件事称作一桩淡红的天光）
F. adj. 淡红（同级比较 as pink as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩清晨淡红的天光相比）
G. adj. 淡红（后置定语 something pink：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 淡红（受程度副词修饰 quite pink：那位旅人的评价）

items.q: a pink coat of the girl
the pinkest coat of the girl anybody
a pink light of the morning
The pinkest light of the morning in

answers.why: pink 意为“粉色”，1978 年向导在旅行手册里记下的是“一件粉色的外套”，此处作前置定语 a pink coat of the girl。
pink 意为“粉色”，此处用比较级 pinker than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
pink 意为“粉色”，旅行手册上 七月 那行字说它是山谷里最粉色的一件，故用最高级 the pinkest coat of the girl。
pink 意为“粉色”，母亲认为这件东西“太粉色了，谁也用不上”，too pink to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
pink 意为“淡红”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩淡红的天光”，此处作前置定语 a pink light of the morning。
pink 意为“淡红”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩清晨淡红的天光一样淡红”，同级比较用 as pink as。
pink 意为“淡红”，旅行手册上那半行字要的是“淡红的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something pink。
pink 意为“淡红”，邻山谷来的那位旅人认为这套计划“相当淡红”，quite 修饰原级 pink。
pink 意为“淡红”，1988 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要淡红”，故用比较级 pinker than。
pink 意为“淡红”，母亲 1990 年说的是“整个山谷里最淡红的那一桩”，故用最高级 the pinkest light of the morning。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1978 年，向导在旅行手册里记下了一件粉色的外套。（a pink coat of the girl）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更粉色。（pinker than …）
母亲觉得它太粉色，谁也用不上。（too pink to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩淡红的天光。（a pink light of the morning）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩清晨淡红的天光一样淡红。（as pink as …）
到了 1985 年，旅行手册上只剩半行字：要的是一件淡红的东西。（something pink）
answers: In 1978 the guide wrote of a pink coat of the girl in the guidebook.
Everybody said it was pinker than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too pink to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a pink light of the morning.
He said nobody would call it as pink as the light of the morning they had once had.
By 1985 the guidebook asked for nothing but something pink.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 pink 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1978 the guide wrote of a pink coat of the girl in the guidebook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the pinkest coat of the girl in the valley, or so the guidebook says.
My mother thought it too pink to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a pink light of the morning, and nobody argued with him.
The traveller from the next valley called the plan quite pink, and everybody laughed.
The pink ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
